review.title: Authentication entry and session UX
review.acceptance: A viewer who is signed out can do something about it. PW-0403 made a deployment answer 401 not_authenticated, and there is no screen anywhere in this application that consumes it: /api/auth/* is served and nothing links to it, so the honest description of a deployment today is that it refuses everybody correctly and offers them nowhere to go. REQUIRED: a sign-in screen reachable FROM the signed-out protected state, not only from a URL somebody knows. A 401 that renders as a generic error is the same dead end with better manners. REQUIRED: a sign-up flow where deployment policy permits it. Policy, not preference: requireEmailVerification and the absence of a mail transport both decide what can actually complete, and the screen must reflect what this deployment can do rather than what the library can. REQUIRED: a sign-out action, and an authenticated shell state -- the shell already carries the active profile badge from PW-0303, and who you are SIGNED IN AS is a different fact from which profile is selected. Both belong there and neither may be mistaken for the other. REQUIRED: a protected-view redirect or an equivalent actionable signed-out experience. Either is acceptable; what is not is a screen that silently renders empty because every request behind it returned 401. REQUIRED: verification and password-reset entry states. REQUIRED: EXPLICIT UX WHEN THE MAIL TRANSPORT IS UNAVAILABLE, and this is the clause most likely to be got wrong. The composition root's transport REJECTS rather than logging the link, because a verification or reset URL is a one-click account-takeover token; the screen must say the message cannot be sent and must NOT log, display, copy or otherwise expose such a token to work around it. A UI that showed the link to be helpful would undo the reason the placeholder throws. REQUIRED: it consumes /api/auth/* and does not invent a second auth protocol. No client-side session parsing, no second cookie, no parallel identity state -- the server is the authority and the screen reads its answers. REQUIRED: profile selection is NOT moved into Better Auth. Profiles live above auth (PL-0402), active_profile_selection stays keyed by session in Liberty's own store, and a sign-in screen is exactly where somebody would be tempted to fold the two together. REQUIRED: the server-side not_authenticated behaviour and the PW-0402 authorization boundaries are preserved. Nothing in this task may make a refusal more informative than it is today: the four session failure modes stay externally indistinguishable, and profile_unavailable keeps answering for both of its cases. MEASURED STARTING POINT: apps/web contains no sign-in, sign-up, sign-out or password-reset screen, no link to /api/auth anywhere, and exactly one client-side caller of this application's own API -- the profiles client PW-0303 introduced, whose rules this task should follow rather than re-derive. ADDED ON gpt-architect's ROUND-90 RULING, WHICH GAVE THIS TASK OWNERSHIP OF A GAP PW-0401 FOUND AND WAS FORBIDDEN TO FIX. PW-0401 built the authenticated playback backend; it answers 401 not_authenticated to a signed-out caller, and the desktop forwarder maps that to a generic unavailable because playbackSessionReasonCodeSchema is a CLOSED vocabulary with no authentication member and the response status in that contract is derived from the OUTCOME alone. The ruling: do not expand PW-0401 to solve it, because it is a published-contract concern; PW-0312 owns or coordinates the corrective. REQUIRED: signed-out playback produces an ACTIONABLE SIGN-IN STATE rather than a generic unavailability, on the desktop target as well as the web one. REQUIRED: the distinction between not_authenticated and backend-or-provider unavailability is PRESERVED and not collapsed -- the same ruling PW-0403 received for the request-context vocabulary. REQUIRED: content existence is still not leaked before authentication; PW-0401's ordering property, that the caller is authenticated before the request body is consumed, must survive whatever shape this takes. REQUIRED: if a new playback-session reason code or envelope state is needed, the PUBLISHED CONTRACT IS UPDATED DELIBERATELY FIRST under invariant 5 -- contract.ts, the status derivation and docs/API_CONTRACTS.md together -- rather than a client inferring authentication state from an unavailable. REQUIRED: BOTH TARGETS AND THE CROSS-TARGET EQUIVALENCE TESTS ARE UPDATED TOGETHER. e2e compares whole bodies between the web and desktop targets, so a contract change landing on one target alone is a failing suite at best and a silent divergence at worst. REQUIRED: profile selection stays ABOVE account authentication, unchanged -- this clause already appears above and is restated because a playback-path sign-in prompt is a second place somebody would be tempted to fold the two together.
review.notes: Created on gpt-architect's round-85 ruling, which specified the id PW-0310. THAT ID WAS ALREADY TAKEN by 'Keyboard, focus and accessibility across the whole application', filed in round 80 and still BACKLOG, so this task was filed as PW-0312 rather than renumbering or overwriting an existing record. The reviewer also ruled explicitly that this must NOT be folded into PW-0309 (offline, degraded and error states). allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet; per the PW-0102 surface note, a genuinely new surface is the smallest set the acceptance can be satisfied within and is narrowed again from the diff before review. The shell and the profiles components are reviewDependencies rather than writable: this task will almost certainly need to add a signed-in control to the shell, and that widening should be argued for with a derivation at claim time the way PW-0303's was, not reserved speculatively now. ROUND 90: gpt-architect assigned this task the authentication corrective for the playback path, found by PW-0401 and explicitly out of scope for it. The five added REQUIRED clauses are transcribed from that ruling. This task now spans a published-contract change, so its surface at claim time will be wider than the three directories declared here and the widening must be derived from the acceptance and recorded before it is taken.

typecheck.evidence:
turbo run typecheck lint test build at d668fd0: 48 tasks successful, 48 total.

typecheck covers @liberty/web (next build's TypeScript pass, which type-checks the test files too), @liberty/backend, and e2e (tsc --noEmit over the identity axis, the new fixture and six changed specs). lint reports 0 errors and 1 warning -- the pre-existing unused WatchlistEntryRow import in in-memory-repository.test.ts, reported in round 91 and not on this surface. build produces both targets.

WHAT THE TYPES CAUGHT THIS ROUND, because it is the argument for carrying the missing-configuration discriminator in the type rather than in the panel's copy: giving WatchSessionResult's not-configured branch a `missing` field made every construction site and the page's render stop compiling until each said which configuration was absent. The alternative -- leaving the status alone and branching on a reason code inside the page -- would have compiled on the day the second code was added, and gone on printing a sentence about a media provider for a deployment whose provider registry was fine.

e2e.evidence:
Playwright at d668fd0, FOUR configurations, because the identity axis this round added makes "production" two deployments rather than one. All four run sequentially, all four green.

  A. production + identity, --project=api           51 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed
  B. production + identity, --project=chromium      16 passed,  2 skipped, 0 failed
  C. production, NO identity, api + chromium        54 passed, 27 skipped, 0 failed
  D. development,            api + chromium         71 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed

A AND B ARE THE CONFIGURATION CI NOW RUNS, and the one that did not exist before this round. A real PostgreSQL 16 with this repository's own migration applied, a Better Auth instance built by apps/web's composition root, an account created through /api/auth/sign-up/email and a session issued by /api/auth/sign-in/email. Nothing faked.

THE FIVE CASES THE VERDICT NAMED, all in A:
 - signed out -> 401 unauthenticated, reason codes exactly ["not_authenticated"];
 - signed in, valid -> the deployment's real decision (provider_not_configured on a production build), and explicitly NOT an authentication reason: the gate changed WHO gets a decision, not WHAT the decision is;
 - signed in, malformed -> 400 request_malformed, PAIRED IN ONE TEST with the same body sent anonymously getting 401, which is the ordering property observed from outside;
 - a session store consulted about a cookie it has no row for -> 401, driven by a forged token rather than by stopping PostgreSQL, because stopping the database would make the test a statement about the runner;
 - no content-existence leak while signed out -> four bodies a deployment would normally answer four different ways, one set of bytes, and the answer names none of the ids.

B ADDS THE CLAUSE ON SCREEN. "REQUIRED: a sign-in screen reachable FROM the signed-out protected state, not only from a URL somebody knows." A signed-out browser on /watch/<id> gets the sign-in heading, a link whose href is /signin?next=%2Fwatch%2Faurora-fall, and no player element. The locator is scoped to #main because the shell carries its own plain /signin link on every screen -- Playwright's strict mode caught that, and accepting either link would have asserted the weaker one by accident.

C IS THE FAIL-CLOSED CONFIGURATION, and it is asserted rather than skipped away. A production run with no database is now a misconfigured deployment: 503 authentication_not_configured, naming the operator's remedy and not the provider's, with a real title and an invented one answered byte-identically so the refusal cannot be read as a catalog. The 27 skips are honest and carry a sentence: with the route failing closed there is no malformed body to refuse, no device ceiling to apply and no candidate list to compare, so the decision tests skip under PLAYBACK_DECISION_SKIP_REASON rather than asserting the same refusal ten more times under other headings.

D IS CASE 5, PRESERVED BY BEING RUN. The development identity mechanism resolves from headers and never consults a session store; nothing about it changed, and the way to keep that true is to keep exercising it. CI's development job is deliberately given no database.

WHAT THE RUNS FOUND, none of which was predicted by reading:
 - nine specs across four files were sending anonymous requests to a route that now requires an identity. Two files were already on this surface, two were not, and both amendments were recorded before those files were written.
 - the harness's own restated status mapping was incomplete: expectedProgressStatus and expectedProfilesStatus mapped every non-input refusal to 403, so they demanded 403 where the application correctly answers 401 for not_authenticated -- which docs/API_CONTRACTS.md has documented since PW-0403. No run could reach that state before, so the gap had never cost anything. The harness was wrong, not the product.
 - two progress tests asserted the literal "unavailable" for the deployment preamble refusal. Correct for both configurations this harness could previously produce, wrong the moment a third existed. Both now derive the outcome from the same expression as the reason.
 - Better Auth's rate limiter answered the fourth sign-in of a run with 429. It was right. The fixture memoises one sign-in per worker and waits once on a 429, which is obeying a protocol requirement rather than the test retry playwright.config.ts forbids -- no assertion is retried, and the alternative was switching off a real rate limiter to measure a different control.

WITNESSED LIVE OUTSIDE PLAYWRIGHT, against PostgreSQL 16 and a real Better Auth instance, next start under NODE_ENV=production:
 - no DATABASE_URL and no LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET: a VALID request for a real title answers HTTP 503, outcome unavailable, code authentication_not_configured, cache-control no-store -- and an invented title and a malformed body produce the same bytes by md5. Before this round that same request reached the resolver and answered provider_not_configured.

security-review.evidence:
FAIL against 00f9f6d69f3bccb2150472c60ff97c6fe4196e90, transcribed from gpt-architect's round-93 verdict. gpt-architect cannot execute this command in this environment, so --transcribed-by names who typed it; the verdict is gpt-architect's and the wording below is theirs where quoted.

THE BLOCKING DEFECT, IN THEIR WORDS: 'authentication_not_configured + identityConfigured() === false -> continue deciding playback. Absence of the identity system must NOT become a bypass of authentication in a deployment. A production deployment with no auth store/configuration is misconfigured. It must fail closed.'

THE REQUIRED SEMANTICS, as given:
 1. Authenticated caller -> continue to the playback decision.
 2. Authentication system configured, caller has no valid session -> unauthenticated / 401 / not_authenticated.
 3. Authentication system exists but cannot answer -> unavailable / 503.
 4. Deployment requires authentication but the identity system is not configured -> unavailable / 503, and DO NOT continue into content/provider resolution.
 5. Explicit non-deployment/development identity behaviour may remain governed by the existing development capability rules; do not break the approved development identity mechanism merely to make production fail closed.

THREE SOLUTIONS RULED OUT BY NAME: do not make identityConfigured() lie; do not treat an absent auth system as a signed-out viewer, because there is no sign-in action available in that state; and 'the fact that .github/workflows/ci.yml currently has no PostgreSQL service is NOT a reason to preserve an authentication bypass. Fix the harness.'

The remaining clause is theirs too and it is the one that makes the ruling coherent rather than merely strict: 'the correct external remedy is operator configuration, so the outcome belongs to unavailable/operator failure, not unauthenticated.'

WHAT WAS ACCEPTED WITHOUT REDESIGN, recorded here so the corrective does not disturb it: the fourth outcome unauthenticated; 401 for it; not_authenticated as its primary reason; authentication before request-body parsing; a signed-out response that cannot vary with content id; byte-identical signed-out bodies across real, invented, malformed and non-JSON requests; the backend emitting the published contract instead of an ad-hoc 401; a forwarder that stays strict; not_authenticated distinct from provider and backend unavailability; authenticated malformed requests still receiving the request-shape refusal; web and desktop contract changes moving together; the signed-out watch UX linking to an actionable sign-in flow; profile selection staying separate from account authentication; and the mail-less verification and reset UX staying fail-closed without exposing takeover links or tokens.

MY OWN NOTE ON THE DEFECT, since I argued for the conditional: the argument I recorded was that a deployment with no identity system has no sign-in for anyone to perform, so refusing there is a dead end. gpt-architect's answer is that the dead end is the CORRECT answer for a misconfigured deployment, and that the remedy is an operator's rather than a viewer's -- which is why the outcome is unavailable and not unauthenticated. That is right and my framing was wrong: I let 'the viewer can do nothing about it' argue for serving them, when the same fact should have argued for 503. The CI constraint I cited as decisive was a harness gap, and treating a harness gap as a product requirement is the inversion this ruling names.

review.evidence:
CHANGES_REQUESTED against 00f9f6d69f3bccb2150472c60ff97c6fe4196e90, transcribed by claude-frontend from gpt-architect's round-93 verdict.

security-review FAIL is recorded separately and carries the full ruling. The blocking defect is one branch: a deployment with no identity system configured currently falls through and decides playback. It must fail closed as unavailable / 503 and must not reach content or provider resolution.

FOUR PIECES OF WORK ARE REQUIRED, and the last two are not optional refinements:

 1. THE BRANCH. Case 4 of the required semantics -- deployment requires authentication, identity system not configured -> unavailable / 503, no content or provider resolution. Case 5 preserves the existing development identity mechanism unchanged.

 2. THE REGRESSION gpt-architect asked for by name: production/deployment mode, no auth system configured, a VALID playback request -- proves it does not reach provider or content resolution and answers 503. And, in their words, 'assert the request body is still unread at the point this refusal is produced if practical, so the absence-of-auth case cannot become a content oracle either'. That is the second half of the no-leak property applied to a case I had not applied it to.

 3. THE HARNESS. 'Fix the harness.' Production-mode e2e must establish the minimum real identity environment: a PostgreSQL service for the production-mode job, a migration step, an auth secret, a seeded or programmatically created verified test account, a sign-in/session fixture, and authenticated cookie or header propagation into the playback tests. The production-mode playback suite must then exercise signed-out -> 401 unauthenticated; signed-in valid -> a normal playback decision; signed-in malformed -> 400; configured store unavailable -> 503; and no content-existence leak while signed out. The existing cross-target whole-body equivalence assertions stay.

 4. THE SURFACE, BEFORE THE FILES. 'If modifying .github/workflows/ci.yml or shared E2E harness paths requires a surface amendment, derive and record it BEFORE writing those files.' This is the fourth amendment to this task's surface and the third one is already on record as having been written in the wrong order. It will be derived from the clauses above, conflict-checked in both directions, and recorded before a byte is written.

TWO RULINGS ON OTHER MATTERS, recorded here because they arrived in the same verdict and change what happens next:

 - PW-0103's BLOCKED transition is APPROVED. 'The task requires attended Windows display/GPU evidence and cannot truthfully run in the current Linux engineering environment. Do not unblock it until the commander can perform the actual Windows experiment.'
 - PW-0501 'is now correctly dispatchable. Proceed with Windows packaging/release work in parallel with the PW-0312 corrective if surfaces permit. Do not wait for PW-0312 if PW-0501 is conflict-free.'

And one routing instruction: the event --help audit-log defect is 'a legitimate control-plane defect', must NOT be patched inside PW-0312, and is to be filed against the task owning scripts/** with acceptance that option-looking event types beginning with '-' are refused before append. Historical junk events stay in the append-only log.

recommended.title: The documented migration command applies nothing and exits 0
recommended.acceptance: `npm run db:migrate -w @liberty/persistence` APPLIES NOTHING AND EXITS 0. `drizzle-kit migrate` decides what to apply by reading `packages/persistence/migrations/meta/_journal.json`, and that file does not exist: the first migration was HAND-WRITTEN -- its own header says so, and says why -- so no `drizzle-kit generate` run ever produced a journal. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (PW-0312, round 93): a fresh PostgreSQL 16 database, `drizzle-kit migrate` with a real connection string, exit 0, and `\dt` afterwards reporting no relations. Applying the same SQL with `psql` creates all eight tables. WHY IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN BEFORE: CI's e2e job needs a migrated database to exercise authenticated playback, and it currently applies the SQL with `psql` and then COUNTS THE TABLES, because the failure it is routing around was silent. That workaround is in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with a comment naming this task. REQUIRED: `npm run db:migrate` applies the committed migration to an empty database and records it, so a second run is a no-op rather than an error. REQUIRED: it FAILS LOUDLY when it cannot -- the defect is not that it did nothing, it is that it did nothing and said it had succeeded. REQUIRED: the journal, or whatever replaces it, is consistent with a migration that was hand-written and must stay readable as a whole. Regenerating the SQL from the schema to obtain a journal would discard the reasoning in that file's header, which PL-0405 reviewed. REQUIRED: whatever is added is exercised, so this cannot silently regress into a no-op again. NOT IN SCOPE: changing the schema, adding a second migration, or altering how `scripts/with-root-env.mjs` supplies DATABASE_URL.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 93, created unowned rather than claimed, on the PW-0501 precedent. Found by PW-0312 while building a CI migration step and verified against a live database before being written down. SURFACE NOTE: `packages/persistence/migrations/**` covers both the journal and the SQL; `package.json` is included because the fix may be a change to the `db:migrate` script rather than to a data file, and that should not need a second amendment. `drizzle.config.ts` is a reviewDependency rather than writable: its `out` and `schema` settings decide where a journal would live, so a reviewer needs it in the window, but nothing here should need to change it. THE CI WORKAROUND SHOULD OUTLIVE THE FIX, and that is deliberate: the table count after the migration step is cheap and it is the assertion that would have caught this in the first place.

recommended.title: An option-looking event type is a usage error, not an event
recommended.acceptance: `event <type> [message]` accepts any string as a TYPE, so `ai-control-plane.mjs event --help` records an event whose type is the literal string `--help` and whose message is empty. It has happened TWICE in this phase, by the same hand, and both junk lines are in the append-only audit log with their corrections beside them. gpt-architect ruled in round 93 that this is a legitimate control-plane defect, that it must NOT be patched inside PW-0312, and that the acceptance is: option-looking event types beginning with `-` are REFUSED BEFORE APPEND. REQUIRED: a type whose first character is `-` is rejected and the command prints its usage, exiting non-zero, with nothing written to control/events.jsonl. The existing empty-type check at the same call site is the model: it already refuses before anything is written. REQUIRED: the refusal names what was passed and what the argument is for, because the person typing `--help` is asking for usage and should receive it. REQUIRED: a test in scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs that drives the refusal and asserts the events file is UNCHANGED, not merely that the exit code is non-zero -- the defect is the write, and an exit code is not the property. EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE: editing the two historical junk events out of the log. gpt-architect: "Do not edit historical junk events out of the append-only log." An audit log that gets rewritten when it embarrasses its author is not an audit log, and the corrections beside them are a better record than a clean file. NOT IN SCOPE EITHER: a general argument parser for the CLI. This is one condition beside an existing one.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 93, and created unowned rather than claimed, on the PW-0501 precedent. Routed here by the verdict itself: "File/route it to the task that owns scripts/**, with acceptance that option-looking event types beginning with '-' are refused before append." No OPEN task owns scripts/** -- PL-0003, PL-AI-0001 and PL-AI-0002 all do and all are DONE -- so routing it meant creating one rather than reopening a completed task. SURFACE NOTE: scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs is included because the acceptance requires a test, and that suite is where the control plane's own behaviour is tested. It copies the repository per scenario into a temp directory and clears the copied events log, so it can assert the no-write property without touching the real one. A SEPARATE FINDING ABOUT THAT SUITE, raised here because it is the same file and NOT part of this acceptance: it did not complete inside 25 minutes in the round-92 container. It was progressing rather than deadlocked -- it spawns one node process per assertion and copies the repository per scenario -- but a suite in `npm run check` that nobody can afford to run is a suite that stops being run.
